chunks: As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Umar ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):
He said: A man came to him and said: "A mouse has fallen into a jar containing ghee or oil. What do you think about eating it?"
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: "Do not eat it."
The man said to him: "The mouse is too insignificant to me to abandon my food on its account."

He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: "You have not shown disrespect to the mouse; rather, you have shown disrespect to your religion. Verily, Allah has forbidden the dead from every thing."

This does not contradict the first report, because the meaning of this report is that when the mouse dies in it, using it is not permitted. But if it exits alive, the ruling is what the first report contained, as the following indicates.

key_terms.اسْتَخْفَفْتَ: you belittled / showed contempt for (Form X verb, expressing wilful disregard)
key_terms.الِانْتِفَاعُ: deriving benefit, usage, utilisation (of a substance)
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةَ: maytah — any creature that dies without lawful ritual slaughter; categorically haram by Quranic decree
key_terms.خَابِيَةٍ: a large earthenware storage jar used for oil, ghee, or water
key_terms.سَمْنٌ: ghee; clarified butter or rendered animal fat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia fiqh on consuming oil or ghee in which a mouse has died, according to Imam al-Baqir (AS) in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) rules that ghee or oil into which a mouse has fallen must not be consumed, grounding the prohibition in Allah's categorical ban on all carrion. When a questioner protests that the mouse is too insignificant to justify discarding his food, the Imam corrects him sharply: the disrespect is not toward the mouse but toward his own religion. Sheikh al-Tusi appends a harmonising gloss, clarifying that this ruling applies specifically when the mouse dies in the substance; if it exits alive, the (more lenient) ruling of the preceding hadith governs.
